slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
To find the perimeter of a polygon from coordinates, use the distance formula on each side and add.

For area, use a formula if the shape is simple (a horizontal base and a vertical height), or enclose the polygon in a rectangle with sides on grid lines and subtract the right triangles around it.

Example: triangle (1, 1), (7, 3), (3, 6). Enclosing rectangle 6 by 5, area 30. Corner triangles: (1/2)(6)(2) = 6, (1/2)(4)(3) = 6, (1/2)(2)(5) = 5. Area = 30 − 17 = 13.
